item.title: How Woven Textiles Are Made
item.description: Describe how cloth takes shape at The Woven Surface, a fictional exhibit with touchable swatches and a working loom. Trace the threads, feel how different structures change the surface, and explain how the weaver controls those effects.

children.definition: The finished lengthwise edge formed during weaving, typically where the crosswise yarn turns back into the cloth.
children.example: On the loom-room swatch, the selvedge feels firm under the thumb, while the cut end sheds threads when rubbed.

children.definition: The set of lengthwise threads held under tension on a loom so that crosswise yarn can be inserted among them.
children.example: On the demonstration loom, the exposed linen warp is taut enough for the weaver to pluck a thread and hear it vibrate.

children.definition: The yarn that runs across the width of woven cloth, passing over and under the lengthwise threads.
children.example: At the touch rail, the soft wool weft forms raised crosswise bands that yield under a fingertip.

children.definition: Having a woven surface on which the lengthwise threads predominate and largely conceal the crosswise threads.
children.example: In the warp-faced ribbon at the entrance, the glossy lengthwise threads hide the grey crosswise yarn until the ribbon is bent.
children.translation_ru: с преобладанием нитей основы на лицевой стороне

children.definition: A weave in which points where the lengthwise and crosswise threads interlace are offset from one row to the next, forming a diagonal pattern.
children.example: In the grey swatch, the twill sends a fine ridge diagonally across the cloth, which you can follow with a fingernail.

children.definition: A structure in which each crosswise thread passes over and under alternate lengthwise threads, reversing that sequence on the next row.
children.example: In the coarse cotton square, the plain weave feels evenly pebbled, and the magnifier shows each crosswise thread going over one lengthwise thread and under the next.

children.definition: A stretch of yarn that passes over two or more adjacent threads of the other set without interlacing with them.
children.example: On the reverse of the silver swatch, you can slip a fingernail under a float that spans four crosswise threads.
children.translation_uz: qarama-qarshi yoʻnalishdagi ikki yoki undan ortiq yonma-yon ip ustidan ular bilan oʻrilishmay oʻtgan ip qismi

children.definition: A figured fabric made on a loom that selects individual lengthwise threads or small groups of them to form a design as the cloth is woven.
children.example: On the indigo jacquard, the smooth arcs stand out against the grainier ground, and the magnifier shows how the threads interlace differently in the two areas.

children.definition: The way the lengthwise and crosswise thread systems pass over and under one another to form a woven structure.
children.example: The enlarged cord model lets you trace the interlacement by touch, following each blue cord where it rises over a white one and dips under the next.

children.definition: The density at which lengthwise threads are arranged for weaving, expressed as a count per unit of width.
children.example: The two strips use the same yarn and weave, but the one woven at the higher sett of thirty warp ends per inch feels firmer when flexed.
collocations: a sett of twenty ends per inch

children.definition: A comb-like loom component with narrow slots that space the lengthwise threads and whose forward movement presses newly inserted crosswise yarn into place.
children.example: At the working loom, the reed makes a dry click as it presses the new row against the woven cloth.

children.definition: One length of weft laid across the warp in a single pass through the opening between the raised and lowered warp threads.
children.example: The weaver inserts one pick of red wool, then stops so visitors can see the single red row against the undyed cloth.
children.translation_ru: уточная нить, проложенная за одну прокидку
children.translation_uz: tanda orasidan bir marta oʻtkazilgan arqoq ipi

children.definition: A short thickened section of otherwise finer yarn, produced deliberately or arising as an irregularity during spinning.
children.example: The unbleached linen feels smooth until your fingertip reaches a slub that bulges from a single crosswise thread.

children.definition: A structure in which separate crosswise yarns are worked back and forth within local areas of colour and packed densely enough to hide the lengthwise threads.
children.example: In the exhibit’s small study of overlapping arcs, the tapestry weave forms a dense surface, with the ochre yarn turning back wherever it meets the blue.
